name: Cutting Chai
steps: Rinse and lightly crush the ginger. Crack the cardamom pods so the seeds are exposed; keep the pods for brewing. Use a deep saucepan with room for the milk to rise.
Bring the water, ginger and cardamom to a boil. Simmer for 2 minutes, then add the tea leaves and boil gently for 2 minutes until the liquid is dark and aromatic.
Add the milk and sugar and stir until dissolved. Bring just to a rising boil, lower the heat immediately and simmer for 3–4 minutes, stirring so the milk does not catch.
When the chai is a rich brown and smells strongly of tea, strain through a fine sieve. Divide into four small heatproof glasses, about 100 ml each, and serve hot.
tips: Cutting means a small serving of strong chai; avoid prolonged boiling after the milk has reduced.
notes: Makes four small cutting glasses. Contains caffeine; ginger suitability follows your household choices.
